proofs.proof_tex:
Assume the stated rational input format and \(2\leq k\leq m\).  First scan the \(mr\) entries of each table, check nonnegativity and the observational and row-wise intervention simplex equalities, and check the \(mr\) inequalities \(e_{is}\geq o_{is}\).  By the compatibility theorem these conditions are necessary and sufficient for \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\neq\varnothing\).  The same scan computes every \(p_i\), after which the reduced coordinates \(a_j,b_j,c_j,d_j,h_j,p_0,g,H\) require \(O(mr+k)\) arithmetic operations.  Since
\[
b_i-\sum_{j\in\mathcal J\setminus\{i\}}h_j=b_i-H+h_i,
\]
the lower endpoint follows from \(H\), \(\sum_j a_j\), and the \(k\) singleton values in a further \(O(k)\) operations.

For the upper endpoint, let \(c_{(1)}\leq\cdots\leq c_{(k)}\).  For each \(2\leq\ell\leq k\),
\[
\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal J:\,|S|=\ell}\sum_{j\in S}c_j
=\sum_{u=1}^{\ell}c_{(u)}.
\]
Indeed, if a cardinality-\(\ell\) set omits an entry no larger than one of its selected entries, exchanging the two cannot increase its sum; finitely many such exchanges leave the \(\ell\) smallest entries.  Consequently,
\[
U(o,e)=\min\left\{g,\min_{j\in\mathcal J}a_j,
\min_{2\leq\ell\leq k}
\frac{\sum_{u=1}^{\ell}c_{(u)}}{\ell-1}\right\}.
\]
Sorting once and scanning prefix sums costs \(O(k\log k)\) arithmetic and comparison operations.  Together with the table scan, this proves the advertised endpoint-evaluation bound and also returns an active upper piece.

We next audit the uncompressed, grid-preserving constructions.  Begin the indicator construction with at most \(m\) positive factual-treatment cells.  Cutting each queried own stratum into factual success and failure introduces at most \(k\) further cells.  For the upper construction, placing the common intersection piece in each of the \(k\) queried factual-success blocks and in the unqueried block introduces at most \(k+1\) further cells, because each application of \(\operatorname{TAKE}\) splits at most one positive-mass cell.  Filling the \(k\) residual coordinate-success demands introduces at most \(k\) more.  Hence the upper indicator law has at most
\[
m+3k+1
\]
positive cells.

For the lower construction, every left vertex has an edge to right block \(0\) and to the \(k-1\) non-diagonal queried right blocks.  Thus there are exactly \(k^2\) possible middle edges.  Realizing every positive edge-flow piece introduces at most \(k^2\) cells, and the residual-failure filling introduces at most one further split for each of the \(k\) left rows.  Including the initial queried own-stratum cuts, the lower indicator law therefore has at most
\[
m+k^2+2k
\]
positive cells.  The lower-flow-attainment lemma supplies the required eligibility invariant: if a left row has positive unused capacity, each adjacent right block is saturated, so its residual demand is filled within the already existing failure union and cannot change the conjunction objective.

Categorical lifting treats one potential-outcome coordinate at a time.  Inside its own factual stratum, assign the first \(r-1\) categorical labels by successive TAKE operations and give the final label the remainder; do the same outside its own stratum.  The corresponding demands are respectively \(o_{is}\) and \(e_{is}-o_{is}\), which are nonnegative by compatibility and sum to the masses of the two domains.  Thus each coordinate introduces at most \(2(r-1)\) cells.  For a queried coordinate, the success indicator already fixes its queried label, and the identical procedure on the indicator-compatible subdomains uses no more splits.  Across all \(m\) coordinates, lifting adds at most \(2m(r-1)\) cells while preserving every prior indicator label.  The TAKE lemma makes no split when a demand or eligible domain has zero mass.  It follows that either endpoint construction has support at most
\[
\max\{m+3k+1,m+k^2+2k\}+2m(r-1)
\leq m+2m(r-1)+k^2+3k+1=N_\star.
\]
The upper- and lower-attainment lemmas and categorical lifting prove that the resulting laws belong to \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\) and attain \(U(o,e)\) and \(L(o,e)\), respectively.

Let \(D\) be the least common multiple of the denominators of the rational input entries.  Every input mass and every reduced coordinate is in \(D^{-1}\mathbb Z\), and
\[
\log_2D\leq\sum \log_2(\text{input denominators})\leq B.
\]
Repeated Euclidean greatest-common-divisor computations and the identity \(\operatorname{lcm}(u,v)=uv/\gcd(u,v)\) compute \(D\) in polynomial bit time.  Indeed, in two consecutive Euclidean remainder steps the smaller positive argument falls by at least a factor of two: if the first remainder is at most half the divisor this is immediate, while otherwise the next remainder is the divisor minus that first remainder and is less than half.  Thus each greatest-common-divisor computation uses a number of schoolbook integer divisions linear in the input bit length, and each such division has polynomial bit cost.  The displayed least-common-multiple division is exact and has a positive integer divisor.
For the lower network, multiply every capacity by \(D\).  Starting from zero, augment along a residual path by its least residual capacity.  Integral capacities imply inductively that every scaled flow is integral.  Scaling back therefore makes every realized edge piece, residual demand, and categorical lifting demand an element of \(D^{-1}\mathbb Z\).  Applying the grid-preservation clause of the TAKE lemma at every refinement proves that every atom of the lower witness has weight in \(D^{-1}\mathbb Z\).

For the upper endpoint, suppose first that the selected active certificate is \(g\) or \(a_j\).  Then \(U(o,e)\in D^{-1}\mathbb Z\).  If instead the selected certificate is a subset \(S\) of size \(\ell\geq2\), then
\[
U(o,e)=\frac{\sum_{j\in S}c_j}{\ell-1}
\in [D(\ell-1)]^{-1}\mathbb Z.
\]
In either case, use the applicable grid for the rest of the upper construction.  The initial values \((U-c_i)_+\), sequential enlargements by the minimum of the remaining demand and remaining capacity, residual-success demands, and categorical lifting demands are all on that grid.  The TAKE lemma therefore keeps every uncompressed upper atom on the same grid.  These arguments establish precisely the denominator claims for the witnesses having support at most \(N_\star\).  They use only addition, subtraction, comparison, and splitting by a requested mass; no conditional probability is formed and no cell mass is a divisor.  On a zero-mass eligible domain every demand is zero and TAKE performs no split.

For completeness, the lower maximum flow is computable with a number of exact operations polynomial in the dimensions and not in the numerical value of \(D\).  The network has \(2k+3\) vertices and \(k^2+2k+1\) forward edges.  Use a breadth-first shortest residual augmenting path at every iteration.  Residual shortest-path distances never decrease; if a directed edge becomes critical, is later restored through its reverse edge, and becomes critical again, the distance to its tail has increased by at least two.  Thus each directed edge is critical only \(O(k)\) times, giving \(O(k^3)\) augmentations and, with an \(O(k^2)\) breadth-first scan, \(O(k^5)\) arithmetic operations.  Scaled capacities are at most \(2D\), and flow additions and subtractions therefore involve \(O(B+\log k)\)-bit integers.  This proves polynomial bit cost for the flow step.

There are only \(O(mr+k^2+k)\) TAKE calls.  A direct finite-cell implementation scans at most \(N_\star\) cells per call, and splitting a cell copies a record containing one treatment label and \(m\) outcome labels.  Hence its operation count is polynomial in \(m,r,k\).  Each uncompressed atom records an \(O(B+\log k)\)-bit rational weight, a treatment label, and \(m\) outcome labels, so the complete primal witness has encoding length polynomial in \(m,r,k,B\).  Zero-mass cells are omitted.  Any rational-linear-algebra pivot used below is chosen only after it is verified nonzero, so zero cells do not create a division there either.

Now apply the certificate-preserving support-compression lemma separately to the two grid-preserving endpoint laws.  It produces, in polynomial time and exact rational arithmetic, a lower law and an upper law with support at most
\[
2mr-m,
\]
the same endpoint value, the same observable and intervention margins, the same active-affine or minimum-cut certificate, and polynomial output encoding length.  This is a second witness guarantee.  Exact kernel cancellation can introduce new rational denominators, so no divisibility by \(D\) or \(D(\ell-1)\) is claimed for the compressed weights.

Finally, a verifier sums the supplied atom weights over each of the \(mr\) observational cells, each of the \(mr\) intervention cells, and the conjunction event.  Its work is polynomial in the displayed support and bit length.  An upper certificate names \(g\), an active margin \(a_j\), or an active subset \(S\); the upper-attainment lemma proves the corresponding affine upper inequality.  A lower certificate names the active zero, total-demand, or singleton cut in
\[
W(o,e)=\min\{H,g,\min_i(H-h_i+g-b_i)\};
\]
the lower-attainment lemma proves the cut value and \(L(o,e)=g-W(o,e)\).  Equality between the checked primal objective and the named dual value certifies endpoint optimality.  One attaining certificate suffices in a tie.  This proves the evaluation, construction, separate support guarantees, grid, certification, zero-boundary, running-time, and bit-complexity assertions.

theorem.statement:
For every \(2\leq k\leq m\) and \(r\geq 1\),
\[
mr\leq s_\star(m,r,k)\leq 2mr-m.
\]
Consequently, \(s_\star(m,r,k)=\Theta(mr)\) uniformly in \(k\).  The upper bound simultaneously controls the separately minimized endpoint supports \(s_L(o,e)\) and \(s_U(o,e)\) for every \((o,e)\in\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\).  The lower bound is witnessed by the compatible family \(o_{is}=1/(mr)\), \(e_{js}=1/r\), for which both endpoint support minima are at least \(mr\).  Hence the quadratic \(k^2\) term in \(N_\star\) is not intrinsic to exact endpoint witnesses.
theorem.proof_tex:
Fix \(2\leq k\leq m\), \(r\geq1\), and \((o,e)\in\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\).  By the sharp-interval theorem, there are finite laws in \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\) attaining \(L(o,e)\) and \(U(o,e)\).  Apply the certificate-preserving support-compression lemma separately to those two laws.  With
\[
R=mr+m(r-1)=2mr-m,
\]
it produces endpoint laws having at most \(R\) positive response atoms.  Therefore, by the definitions of the two separate endpoint support minima,
\[
s_L(o,e)\leq 2mr-m,
\qquad
s_U(o,e)\leq 2mr-m.
\]
Taking their maximum and then the supremum over \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\) gives
\[
s_\star(m,r,k)
=\sup_{(o,e)\in\mathcal C_{m,r,k}}
  \max\{s_L(o,e),s_U(o,e)\}
\leq 2mr-m.
\]
This is one uniform bound for both endpoint minima; in particular, it does not choose a different margin family according to which endpoint is under consideration.

For the reverse inequality, use the forced-positive-cell construction
\[
o_{is}=\frac{1}{mr}
\quad(i\in\mathcal X, s\in\mathcal Y),
\qquad
e_{js}=\frac{1}{r}
\quad(j\in\mathcal X, s\in\mathcal Y).
\]
There are \(mr\) observational cells, so \(\sum_{i,s}o_{is}=1\), and for each \(j\), \(\sum_s e_{js}=1\).  Thus the observational table and every intervention row satisfy their respective simplex restrictions.  Moreover, \(m\geq2\) implies
\[
e_{is}=\frac1r\geq\frac1{mr}=o_{is}
\qquad(i\in\mathcal X, s\in\mathcal Y).
\]
The compatibility theorem now yields \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\neq\varnothing\), so this pair lies in \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\).

Let \(Q\in\mathcal Q(o,e)\).  For \(i\in\mathcal X\) and \(s\in\mathcal Y\), define the response-table cell
\[
C_{is}=\{(x,y_1,\ldots,y_m)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y^m:x=i, y_i=s\}.
\]
The \(mr\) cells \(C_{is}\) are pairwise disjoint.  The observational-margin restriction in the definition of \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\) gives
\[
Q(C_{is})=\Pr_Q(X=i,Y_i=s)=o_{is}=\frac1{mr}>0.
\]
Since the response space is finite, the support of \(Q\) must contain at least one atom in every \(C_{is}\).  Disjointness then gives
\[
\sigma(Q)\geq mr.
\]
The sharp-interval theorem makes both endpoint-constrained sets in the definitions of \(s_L(o,e)\) and \(s_U(o,e)\) nonempty.  The last inequality holds for every law in either set, and hence
\[
s_L(o,e)\geq mr,
\qquad
s_U(o,e)\geq mr.
\]
Using this single compatible family in the supremum defining \(s_\star\) proves \(s_\star(m,r,k)\geq mr\).

Combining the two directions,
\[
mr\leq s_\star(m,r,k)\leq2mr-m\leq2mr.
\]
The constants \(1\) and \(2\) do not depend on \(k\), so the order is \(\Theta(mr)\) uniformly over \(2\leq k\leq m\).  Because \(N_\star=m+2m(r-1)+k^2+3k+1\) contains a quadratic term in \(k\), whereas every endpoint has an exact witness with at most \(2mr-m\) atoms, that quadratic term is an overhead of the grid-preserving flow construction rather than an intrinsic uniform support requirement.
theorem.justification: Finite-rank certificate-preserving compression and a forced-positive-cell family give matching linear order in the number of observational cells.
theorem.gap: This closes the support-order question and separates intrinsic endpoint support from the quadratic overhead of the explicit grid-preserving flow witness.
theorem.consumer: An exact categorical audit can use a constructively compressed endpoint witness with at most \(2mr-m\) atoms; the \(N_\star\) witness is needed only when preservation of the input denominator grid is desired.

prose_updates.tldr: Common-population observational and single-treatment intervention margins determine the exact identified interval for every finite-alphabet scalar conjunction probability of causation.  The Shu--Wang--Li endpoints are attained for every compatible real input by indicator coarsening, upper intersection packing, and a deleted-diagonal lower flow with a residual-failure invariant.  For rational inputs, sorting evaluates the endpoints and explicit laws of support at most \(N_\star\) preserve the relevant input denominator grid.  A separate exact margin-kernel step preserves the active-affine or minimum-cut certificate while constructively compressing either endpoint law to at most \(2mr-m\) atoms of polynomial encoding length; no denominator-divisibility claim is made after compression.  Thus \(mr\leq s_\star(m,r,k)\leq2mr-m\), and block-multinomial confidence-region inversion supplies uniform finite-sample coverage while Cheng--Mao--Pearl--Li retain credit for directional inference.

project_justification.gap: Shu--Wang--Li prove the scalar formulas but leave all-dimensional pointwise tightness open; Xie--Li's constructive proof is binary; and generic response-signature programs hide the scalar geometry in exponentially many columns while supplying neither the sorted endpoint evaluator nor a certificate-preserving linear-support construction.
project_justification.niche: The common-population scalar conjunction problem has two complementary finite structures: factual failures delete diagonal flow edges, and every endpoint-optimal response law is flat along any feasible kernel direction of the \(2mr-m\) retained margin rows.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives exact categorical lifting, packing and flow endpoint laws, sorted and min-cut dual certificates, grid-preserving polynomial witnesses of support at most \(N_\star\), constructive certificate-preserving compression to at most \(2mr-m\) atoms, a matching \(mr\) support lower family, and boundary-safe finite-sample inversion.

prose_updates.related_work: Shu--Wang--Li Theorem 2 supplies the scalar affine formulas and leaves their general-dimensional tightness unresolved.  Xie--Li Theorem 3.2 is the closest constructive precedent, solving the binary eight-cell system.  Koperberg Proposition 6 supplies a finite Hall--Strassen coupling principle adapted to the deleted-diagonal lower network.  Tian--Pearl supplies the binary PNS interval used only as an algebraic sanity check, and Li--Pearl gives earlier recursive multivalued bounds.  Rossetto--Antonucci provides a generic sharp response-signature linear program and SCM realization; the present scalar geometry instead yields sorted endpoint evaluation, explicit active-affine or minimum-cut certificates, grid-preserving witnesses, and constructive certificate-preserving \(O(mr)\)-support compression.  Cheng--Mao--Pearl--Li provides active-set directional limit theory and is credited rather than relabeled.  Horowitz--Lee, Stoye, and Kaido--Molinari--Stoye motivate confidence-region and projection inference, while the finite-sample result here is specialized to the block-multinomial margin polytope.  Harinen and coauthors provide the hypothetical common-population customer-journey setting in which a prespecified multichannel response-pattern probability is a concrete scalar consumer.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Scalar sharpness does not imply simultaneous sharpness for several response patterns, so separately summing scalar endpoint values can yield an unattainable policy utility.  The confidence interval is a conservative outer inversion and has no optimal-width claim.  The endpoint-support frontier satisfies \(mr\leq s_\star(m,r,k)\leq2mr-m\), hence has exact order \(mr\), but the exact worst-case constant remains open.  Divisibility by \(D\) or \(D(\ell-1)\) belongs only to the original grid-preserving witnesses of support at most \(N_\star\); the compressed witnesses have polynomial-bit rational weights with no asserted denominator divisor.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The finite max-flow/min-cut theorem, multinomial concentration, and exact rational linear algebra are standard inputs.  The proved contribution is all-alphabet categorical lifting, upper and lower endpoint attainment, the residual-failure invariant, exact interval equality, the grid and bit audit, and constructive certificate-preserving compression.  Unequal alphabets and repeated queried labels are covered, but factual-conditioned representative probabilities of causation, incomplete subpopulations, mediator restrictions, population mismatch, and simultaneous vectors of conjunctions are outside the theorem.  The Tian--Pearl binary reduction is an unnumbered sanity corollary, not a research-target theorem.  For \(k=1\), the target is the known margin \(a_1\); for \(r=1\), the identified interval is \([1,1]\).  The support frontier has proved order \(mr\), with lower bound \(mr\) and constructive upper bound \(2mr-m\); only the exact constant remains unresolved.  The larger \(N_\star\) support guarantee is retained solely for its stronger denominator-grid property.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(\Omega=\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y^m\).  Because \(\mathcal X\) and \(\mathcal Y\) are finite, every law on \(\Omega\) has finite support.  We use finite-dimensional kernel cancellation.  For \(\omega=(x,y_1,\ldots,y_m)\in\Omega\), define the zero-one margin matrix \(M\) by the \(mr\) observational rows
\[
 M^{\mathrm{obs}}_{is}(\omega)=\mathbf 1\{x=i,\ y_i=s\},
 \qquad i\in\mathcal X,\ s\in\mathcal Y,
\]
and the \(m(r-1)\) intervention rows
\[
 M^{\mathrm{int}}_{js}(\omega)=\mathbf 1\{y_j=s\},
 \qquad j\in\mathcal X,\ s\in\{1,\ldots,r-1\}.
\]
When \(r=1\), the second family is empty.  Thus \(M\) has
\[
 R=mr+m(r-1)=2mr-m
\]
rows.  The observational rows satisfy, column by column,
\[
 \sum_{i\in\mathcal X}\sum_{s\in\mathcal Y}
 M^{\mathrm{obs}}_{is}(\omega)=1.
\]
It follows that \(Mv=0\) implies \(\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}v_\omega=0\).  Hence preserving \(MQ\) preserves total mass, all observational cells, and all intervention cells with labels \(1,\ldots,r-1\).  It also preserves the omitted intervention cell for every \(j\), because
\[
 \Pr_Q(Y_j=r)=1-\sum_{s=1}^{r-1}\Pr_Q(Y_j=s).
\]
Consequently, by the definition of \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\), every nonnegative vector with the same image under \(M\) as a member of \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\) is another member of \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\).  Potential-outcome consistency is unchanged because each column remains an atom \((x,y_1,\ldots,y_m)\) with factual outcome \(y_x\).

Define the query row
\[
 z(\omega)=\mathbf 1\{y_j=s_j^\star\text{ for every }j\in\mathcal J\}.
\]
Then the conjunction probability under \(Q\) is \(z^\top Q\).  Fix \(t\in\{L(o,e),U(o,e)\}\) and an endpoint law \(Q_0\in\mathcal Q(o,e)\) with \(z^\top Q_0=t\).  At any stage let \(Q\) be the current endpoint law and let
\[
 S=\{\omega\in\Omega:Q_\omega>0\}.
\]
If \(|S|>R\), the columns of the \(R\)-row matrix \(M_S\) are linearly dependent.  Choose a nonzero vector \(v\), supported on \(S\), such that \(Mv=0\).  Since every \(Q_\omega\) with \(\omega\in S\) is strictly positive, there is \(\varepsilon>0\) such that both \(Q+\varepsilon v\) and \(Q-\varepsilon v\) are nonnegative.  Both perturbations have total mass one and the same required margins, so both belong to \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\).

We now use endpoint optimality supplied by the sharp-interval theorem.  If \(t=L(o,e)\) and \(z^\top v\neq0\), one of the two feasible perturbations has conjunction probability
\[
 t-\varepsilon|z^\top v|<L(o,e),
\]
contradicting that \(L(o,e)\) is the minimum over \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\).  If \(t=U(o,e)\), the opposite choice of sign has conjunction probability
\[
 t+\varepsilon|z^\top v|>U(o,e),
\]
contradicting maximality.  Therefore
\[
 z^\top v=0
\]
at either endpoint.  This is the step that avoids adding the query row to the rank count.

Because \(Mv=0\) gives \(\sum_\omega v_\omega=0\), the nonzero vector \(v\) has both a positive and a negative coordinate.  Define
\[
 \lambda=\min_{\omega\in S:\,v_\omega>0}\frac{Q_\omega}{v_\omega}>0,
 \qquad Q'=Q-\lambda v.
\]
The minimum is taken only over strictly positive coordinates of \(v\), so no division by zero occurs.  Its indexed weights \(Q_\omega\) are also strictly positive by the definition of \(S\).  The choice of \(\lambda\) gives \(Q'\geq0\), makes at least one formerly positive weight zero, and creates no positive weight outside \(S\).  Moreover,
\[
 MQ'=MQ-\lambda Mv=MQ,
 \qquad
 z^\top Q'=z^\top Q-\lambda z^\top v=t.
\]
Thus \(Q'\) is another endpoint-attaining member of \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\) with strictly smaller support.  Iteration terminates after at most \(\sigma(Q_0)-R\) cancellations and returns \(Q_{\mathrm c}\) satisfying
\[
 \sigma(Q_{\mathrm c})\leq R=2mr-m.
\]
If the initial support is already at most \(R\), no cancellation is needed.  Zero-mass atoms never enter \(S\), so all zero-cell boundary cases are covered.

An active-affine upper certificate is an inequality determined by the fixed margins whose value equals \(U(o,e)\), and a deleted-diagonal minimum-cut certificate is likewise determined by the fixed capacities and has value \(L(o,e)\) after the identity \(L=g-W\).  Kernel cancellation changes neither the margins nor the attained value \(t\).  The same active subset or minimum cut therefore remains a valid equality certificate for \(Q_{\mathrm c}\).

Finally suppose that \(Q_0\) is supplied as a rational sparse list.  At a stage with more than \(R\) active atoms, rational Gaussian elimination on the zero-one matrix \(M_S\) finds a dependent column and a maximal independent subfamily expressing it.  The resulting kernel vector is supported on at most \(R+1\) columns.  Clearing denominators by the signed-minor construction gives a nonzero integer vector \(v\).  To bound it without an external theorem, expand any \(q\)-by-\(q\) zero-one minor by the Leibniz formula.  It is a sum of \(q!\) terms, each belonging to \(\{-1,0,1\}\), and hence its absolute value is at most \(q!\).  Since \(q\leq R\), every coordinate of \(v\) therefore has bit length at most \(1+\lceil\log_2(R!)\rceil=O(R\log(R+1))\).

If the current weights have common positive denominator \(D_0\), and \(\omega_0\) realizes the minimum in the definition of \(\lambda\), then, writing \(Q_{\omega}=n_\omega/D_0\),
\[
 Q'_\omega
 =\frac{n_\omega v_{\omega_0}-n_{\omega_0}v_\omega}
 {D_0v_{\omega_0}}.
\]
Thus one cancellation increases the common-denominator bit length by at most \(O(R\log(R+1))\); since all weights remain in \([0,1]\), the numerator bit lengths satisfy the same polynomial bound.  There are at most \(\sigma(Q_0)-R\) iterations.  Gaussian elimination, exact ratio comparison, and each vector update are polynomial in the current sparse-list length and bit length.  Hence the entire cancellation procedure has running time and output encoding length polynomial in the encoding length of \(Q_0\), \(m\), and \(r\).  The extra factors \(|v_{\omega_0}|\) in successive denominators show why this argument asserts polynomial bit length but makes no denominator-divisibility claim for the compressed weights.

Fix \(2\leq k\leq m\) and \(r\geq1\).  First let \((o,e)\in\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\).  By the sharp-interval theorem, there exist laws \(Q_L,Q_U\in\mathcal Q(o,e)\) such that
\[
 Q_L\!\left(\bigcap_{j\in\mathcal J}A_j\right)=L(o,e),
 \qquad
 Q_U\!\left(\bigcap_{j\in\mathcal J}A_j\right)=U(o,e).
\]
Apply the certificate-preserving endpoint-compression lemma separately to \(Q_L\) and \(Q_U\).  It gives endpoint laws with support at most
\[
 mr+m(r-1)=2mr-m.
\]
By the definitions of the separate endpoint support minima,
\[
 s_L(o,e)\leq2mr-m,
 \qquad
 s_U(o,e)\leq2mr-m.
\]
Taking their maximum and then the supremum over \((o,e)\in\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\) yields
\[
 s_\star(m,r,k)\leq2mr-m.
\]

For the reverse inequality, use the forced-positive-cell construction
\[
 o_{is}=\frac1{mr}
 \quad(i\in\mathcal X,\ s\in\mathcal Y),
 \qquad
 e_{js}=\frac1r
 \quad(j\in\mathcal X,\ s\in\mathcal Y).
\]
The observational entries are nonnegative and sum to one, and every intervention row is nonnegative and sums to one.  Since \(m\geq k\geq2\), in particular \(m\geq1\), and therefore
\[
 e_{is}=\frac1r\geq\frac1{mr}=o_{is}
\]
for all \(i\in\mathcal X\) and \(s\in\mathcal Y\).  The compatibility theorem implies that this pair belongs to \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\).

Let \(Q\in\mathcal Q(o,e)\) be arbitrary.  For \(i\in\mathcal X\) and \(s\in\mathcal Y\), define the observational cell
\[
 C_{is}=\{(x,y_1,\ldots,y_m)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y^m:x=i,\ y_i=s\}.
\]
These \(mr\) cells are pairwise disjoint and exhaust \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y^m\).  The defining observational-margin restriction for \(\mathcal Q(o,e)\) gives
\[
 Q(C_{is})=o_{is}=\frac1{mr}>0.
\]
Because the sample space is finite, the support of \(Q\) must contain at least one atom in each positive-mass cell.  Disjointness of the cells therefore implies
\[
 \sigma(Q)\geq mr.
\]
The sharp-interval theorem ensures that both endpoint faces are nonempty, and the preceding inequality applies to every law on either face.  Hence
\[
 s_L(o,e)\geq mr,
 \qquad
 s_U(o,e)\geq mr.
\]
The definition of the supremum frontier now gives \(s_\star(m,r,k)\geq mr\).  Combining the bounds,
\[
 mr\leq s_\star(m,r,k)\leq2mr-m\leq2mr,
\]
so \(s_\star(m,r,k)=\Theta(mr)\) with constants independent of \(k\).  Finally,
\[
 N_\star=m+2m(r-1)+k^2+3k+1=(2mr-m)+k^2+3k+1,
\]
whereas every compatible pair has exact lower- and upper-endpoint witnesses supported on at most \(2mr-m\) atoms.  Thus the quadratic term in \(N_\star\) is not intrinsic to exact endpoint support.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(2\leq k\leq m\) and \(r\geq1\),
\[
 mr\leq s_\star(m,r,k)\leq 2mr-m.
\]
Consequently \(s_\star(m,r,k)=\Theta(mr)\) uniformly in \(k\).  The upper bound simultaneously controls the two separately minimized endpoint supports \(s_L(o,e)\) and \(s_U(o,e)\) for every \((o,e)\in\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\).  The lower bound is witnessed by the compatible family \(o_{is}=1/(mr)\), \(e_{js}=1/r\), for which both endpoint support minima are at least \(mr\).  Hence the quadratic \(k^2\) term in \(N_\star\) is not intrinsic to exact endpoint witnesses.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The accepted endpoint-face kernel cancellation uses only the \(mr+m(r-1)=2mr-m\) margin rows and preserves the endpoint query, so the former upper bound \(2mr-m+1\) must be tightened to \(2mr-m\).
